supino.p: Lie on the bench with your eyes just below the bar. Feet planted, glutes and head on the bench. Pull your shoulder blades together and down, making a small natural arch in your back. Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width, wrists straight over the forearms.
s: Unrack the bar with straight arms and bring it over your shoulders.
Lower the bar under control until it lightly touches the lower chest, near the nipple line.
Keep your elbows at 45–70° from your torso, neither tucked tight nor flared to 90°.
Press the bar up and slightly back toward your shoulders until your arms are almost straight.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench from start to finish.
supino.r: Breathe in before lowering and hold it with your abs braced; breathe out once you pass the hardest part of the press.
supino.a: Lower in 2–3 seconds and press with intent. Use the full range: the bar touches your chest.
supino.f: Chest, helped by the front of the shoulder and the triceps.
d: Think about pushing your body away from the bar, driving your back into the bench.
Use a spotter or the rack safeties with heavy loads.
e: Lifting your glutes off the bench to move more weight.
Bouncing the bar off your chest.
Flaring the elbows to 90°, which stresses the shoulder.
supino.c: If your shoulder hurts, narrow your grip and tuck your elbows a bit, or switch to dumbbells with a neutral grip.

v.b.in: Bench at about 30°: the weight comes down higher, on the upper chest near the collarbones.
v.b.de: Decline bench: lock your legs in and lower the weight to the lower chest.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: lower until you feel your chest stretch, dumbbells beside the chest, and press them together without clanking.
v.e.sm: Smith: set the bench so the bar lands on the lower chest; the track guides you, so focus on controlling the descent.
v.e.ma: Machine: set the seat so the handles are level with mid-chest.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: shorter range and more chest; don't overdo the width, to spare your shoulders.
v.w.fe: Close grip (shoulder width): elbows closer to the body, more triceps.
v.g.ne: Neutral grip with dumbbells (palms facing each other): usually the most shoulder-friendly.
v.g.su: Reverse grip: hold tight and lower the bar a bit lower on the chest; use a spotter.

crucifixo.p: Lying on the bench (or seated on the machine, or standing between cables), arms open with elbows slightly bent. Shoulder blades together and down, chest up.
s: Start with your arms in front of your chest, hands almost touching.
Open your arms in an arc, like hugging a big tree, without changing the elbow angle.
Lower until you feel your chest stretch, hands roughly at shoulder height.
Bring your arms back together along the same arc, squeezing your chest at the end.
crucifixo.r: Breathe in as your arms open and out as they close.
crucifixo.a: Open slowly over 2–3 seconds and pause briefly with your chest stretched.
crucifixo.f: Chest, especially near the armpits when the arms are open.
d: Think about bringing your elbows together, not your hands.
Use moderate loads: the long arm makes the weight feel much heavier.
e: Bending and straightening the elbows during the rep (it turns into a press).
Going too deep and straining the front of the shoulder.
Clanking the dumbbells at the top and losing tension.
crucifixo.c: Stop the descent before you feel pressure in the front of the shoulder.

v.b.in: Incline: arms travel toward your face, focusing on the upper chest.
v.b.de: Decline (or high-to-low cable): hands close at belly height, focusing on the lower chest.
v.e.po: Cable (crossover): step forward, lean your torso slightly and bring your hands together in front; tension stays on at the end.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: tension fades near the top, so you don't need to bring your arms all the way together.
v.e.ma: Pec deck: set the seat so the handles are at chest height and keep your back on the pad.
v.l.un: One arm: hold on with the other hand so your torso doesn't twist.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time, keeping the other still in front.

landmine.p: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or landmine base. Stand (or kneel) facing it, holding the free end at chest height, torso braced and leaning slightly forward.
s: Hold the end of the bar with one or both hands, close to your chest.
Press the bar up and forward, following its natural arc.
Straighten your arms and let your shoulder blades move forward a little at the end.
Lower slowly back to chest height.
landmine.r: Breathe out as you press and in as you lower.
landmine.a: Controlled, 2 seconds on the way down.
landmine.f: Upper chest and front of the shoulder, with triceps and serratus helping.
d: Squeeze your glutes and abs so your lower back doesn't arch.
A great option for anyone who feels their shoulder in a regular overhead press.
e: Arching the lower back to press.
Letting the elbow flare out too far.
landmine.c: Secure the base of the bar so it can't slip.

v.l.un: One arm: stand with the opposite leg forward and don't let your torso rotate.
v.l.al: Alternating: switch hands each rep while keeping your torso still.

flexao.p: Hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders, fingers forward. Body straight from head to heels, abs and glutes tight.
s: Lower your whole body as one plank, bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows at about 45° from your body.
Go down until your chest almost touches the floor.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight, keeping your body aligned.
flexao.r: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
flexao.a: 2 seconds down, firm push up. Full range: chest close to the floor.
flexao.f: Chest, triceps and front of the shoulder; your abs work to hold the plank.
d: If you can't do full reps, put your hands on a bench (hands elevated) rather than dropping to your knees.
To make it harder, elevate your feet or put a plate on your back.
e: Letting the hips sag or pike up.
Doing half reps without going down.
flexao.c: If your wrists bother you, use push-up handles or dumbbells to keep them straight.

v.b.pe: Feet elevated: more load on the arms and more upper chest; keep your hips in line.
v.b.ma: Hands elevated (on a bench or bar): an easier version, great for starting out.
v.w.ab: Wide hands: more chest and a shorter range; don't overdo it, to spare your shoulders.
v.w.fe: Close hands (diamond): elbows tucked against the body, much more triceps.
v.e.bo: Stability ball: hands on the ball, demands more shoulder and core stability; go slowly.
v.e.tr: Suspended (TRX/rings): the more your body leans, the harder it gets; don't let your arms drift apart.

mergulho.p: Support yourself on the parallel bars with straight arms, shoulders down and away from your ears, body hanging.
s: Bend your elbows and lower your body under control.
Go down until your elbows are near 90°, or as far as your shoulders are comfortable.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulders down throughout.
mergulho.r: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
mergulho.a: 2–3 seconds down, no bouncing at the bottom.
mergulho.f: Triceps and chest, especially the lower part, plus the front of the shoulder.
d: Cross your legs behind you so your body doesn't swing.
When it gets easy, add weight with a dip belt.
e: Going too deep and feeling shoulder pain.
Letting your shoulders rise toward your ears.
mergulho.c: If you have a history of shoulder pain, start on the assisted machine with a shorter range.

v.p.fr: Leaning forward with elbows a bit wider: more chest.
v.e.ma: Machine or assisted: the counterweight helps; reduce the assistance gradually.
v.e.bc: Bench dip: hands on a bench behind you, hips close to the bench and feet in front. Don't go too deep, because this position strains the front of the shoulder.

desenv.p: Seated with your back supported (or standing, feet hip-width apart), load at shoulder height, elbows slightly in front of your body, wrists straight, abs braced.
s: Press the load straight up overhead.
At the top, the load is stacked over your shoulders and slightly behind your head.
Straighten your arms almost fully without forcefully locking out.
Lower under control to chin or ear height.
desenv.r: Breathe in at the bottom, hold it with your abs braced and breathe out once past the hard part of the press.
desenv.a: 2 seconds down. Lower until your hands are near your shoulders.
desenv.f: Front and middle of the shoulder, with triceps helping.
d: Squeeze your glutes and abs so your back doesn't arch.
With a barbell, move your face out of the way on the way up and bring your head back under the bar at the top.
e: Arching the lower back a lot.
Not lowering enough and cutting the range short.
Letting the elbows drift far behind the body.
desenv.c: If your shoulder hurts, use a neutral grip or the landmine press.

v.e.ba: Barbell: grip slightly wider than your shoulders and keep the bar close to your face.
v.e.ma: Machine: set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
v.e.sm: Smith: position the bench so the bar comes down in front of your face, not behind your head.
v.p.pe: Standing: demands more from your abs and glutes; don't lean your torso back.
v.g.ne: Neutral grip (palms facing each other): usually more comfortable for the shoulders.
v.g.ar: Arnold: start with palms facing you and rotate them forward as you press.
v.l.un: One arm: hold on firmly with the other hand and don't lean to the side.
v.l.al: Alternating: press one arm while the other stays still at the bottom.

elevfront.p: Standing, feet hip-width apart, load in front of your thighs, arms almost straight, abs braced.
s: Raise your arms in front of you with elbows slightly bent.
Stop when your hands reach shoulder height.
Hold for a moment at the top.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.
elevfront.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
elevfront.a: Up in 1–2 s, down in 2–3 s.
d: Use light to moderate loads: the long arm makes it heavy.
Think about reaching forward, not up.
elevfront.c: This muscle already works a lot in pressing; don't overdo the volume.

v.e.po: Cable: stand with your back to a low pulley, cable passing between your legs; tension stays constant.
v.e.an: Plate: hold it on both sides, like a steering wheel.
v.g.su: Underhand grip (palms up): works a bit of biceps too.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time without twisting your torso.
v.l.un: One arm: hold onto a support with the other hand.

pike.p: Start in a push-up position and walk your feet toward your hands, making an upside-down V with your hips high. Hands shoulder-width apart.
s: Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor, slightly in front of your hands.
Keep your hips high throughout.
Go down until your head almost touches the floor.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
pike.r: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
d: A stepping stone toward the handstand push-up.
The more vertical your torso, the harder it is.
e: Letting the hips drop so it becomes a regular push-up.
Flaring the elbows out to the sides.
Hitting your head on the floor.
pike.c: Start with few reps: your head is below your heart and you may get dizzy.

v.b.pe: Feet elevated on a bench: the torso is more vertical and the exercise gets heavier.

elevlat.p: Standing, feet hip-width apart, dumbbells at your sides, torso leaning slightly forward, elbows slightly bent.
s: Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your arms are parallel to the floor, at shoulder height.
Keep your elbows level with or slightly above your hands.
Lower slowly, without letting the weights touch your thighs.
elevlat.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
elevlat.a: Up in 1–2 s, down in 2–3 s. Light loads and moderate to high reps work well.
d: Think about pushing the weights away from your body, out to the sides.
Bringing the arms slightly forward (in the plane of the shoulder blade) is usually more comfortable.
e: Lifting your hands above your elbows.
elevlat.c: If you feel pinching at the top, stop a little below shoulder level.

v.e.po: Cable: cable from the low pulley on the opposite side; tension is higher at the bottom of the movement.
v.e.ma: Machine: line your shoulder up with the machine's pivot and push with your elbow.
v.e.el: Band: stand on the band; tension increases at the top.
v.p.la: Leaning to the side: hold a support and lean away; works the bottom of the movement more.
v.p.ld: Lying on your side on an incline bench: more tension at the start of the movement.
v.p.ct: Cable behind the body: the arm starts further back, with the muscle more stretched.
v.c.fl: Elbow bent to 90°: the weight is closer to the shoulder and you can use more load.
v.l.un: One arm: hold onto a support with the other hand.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

yraise.p: Face the cable stack holding the cables (or cable ends) crossed at hip height, arms straight and slightly forward, torso leaning slightly.
s: Raise your arms up and out, making a Y shape with your body.
Lead with your thumbs pointing up and back.
Stop when your arms are overhead, beside your ears.
Lower slowly to the start.
yraise.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
yraise.a: Slow and controlled, very light load.
yraise.f: Lower traps (middle of the back) and shoulders.
d: Think about bringing your shoulder blades down and back as your arms rise.
Very light load: the goal is control.
e: Using too much weight and swinging.
yraise.c: Great for shoulder health; no need for heavy loads.

v.e.ha: Lying face down on an incline bench: let your arms hang and raise them in a Y with very light dumbbells.

iyt.p: Lie face down on an incline bench (or the floor), arms hanging down, thumbs up.
s: I: raise your straight arms in front, in line with your body.
Y: raise your arms diagonally, making a Y.
T: open your arms out to the sides, making a T.
Do the reps for each letter in sequence, always slowly.
iyt.r: Breathe out as your arms rise and in as they lower.
iyt.a: Slow, with a 1-second hold at the top of each rep.
iyt.f: Middle and lower traps, back of the shoulder and the muscles around the shoulder blade.
d: Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down before lifting your arms.
Start with no weight or 1–2 kg.
e: Lifting your chest off the bench to gain height.
iyt.c: A light exercise, good as a warm-up or for posture.

v.e.co: No weight: ideal for learning and warming up.

tbrucos.p: Lie face down on a flat or incline bench, arms hanging, holding light dumbbells, thumbs up.
s: Pull your shoulder blades together before moving your arms.
Open your arms out to the sides to shoulder level, making a T.
Hold for 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly.
tbrucos.r: Breathe out as your arms open and in as you lower.
tbrucos.a: Slow, with a pause at the top.
tbrucos.f: Middle of the back (middle traps, rhomboids) and back of the shoulder.
d: Keep your chin slightly tucked and your neck relaxed.
Light load; the focus is squeezing the shoulder blades.
e: Bending the elbows a lot and turning it into a row.
tbrucos.c: Great for anyone who sits a lot.

v.e.co: No weight: good for learning the shoulder blade movement.

remalta.p: Standing, holding the load in front of your thighs, grip shoulder-width or slightly wider, arms straight.
s: Pull the load up close to your body, driving your elbows up and out.
Your elbows always stay higher than your hands.
Lift to mid-chest height, elbows level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
remalta.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
remalta.f: Middle of the shoulder and traps.
d: A wider grip tends to be more comfortable for the shoulders.
No need to go above shoulder level.
e: Using a very narrow grip and pulling to the chin, which pinches the shoulder.
Letting the hands rise higher than the elbows.
remalta.c: If you feel pinching in the shoulder, widen your grip and lift less.

v.e.bw: EZ bar: more comfortable for the wrists.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: each arm follows its natural path; usually more comfortable.
v.e.po: Low cable with a bar or rope: constant tension.
v.e.sm: Smith: the track guides you; focus on driving the elbows out.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: more side delt and more comfortable.
v.w.fe: Narrow grip: more traps, but it pinches the shoulder more; lift less.

crucinv.p: Seated on the reverse pec deck with your chest on the pad (or bent over with dumbbells), arms straight in front at shoulder height.
s: Open your arms back in an arc, elbows slightly bent.
Bring your hands in line with your body.
Hold for a moment.
Return slowly to the front.
crucinv.r: Breathe out as you open and in as you return.
crucinv.a: Slow movement; light to moderate load.
d: Think about sending your hands far out to the sides, not about squeezing your shoulder blades.
Leaving the shoulder blades free focuses more on the rear delts.
crucinv.c: Small muscle: heavy loads only ruin your technique.

v.e.ha: Dumbbells: torso bent forward, almost parallel to the floor, back straight.
v.e.po: Cables: hold the cables crossed and open your arms; constant tension.
v.e.el: Band: hold it in front at chest height and open your arms.
v.p.in: Chest supported on an incline bench: takes the lower back out of it.
v.p.pe: Standing bent over: keep your back straight.
v.p.cr: Crossed cables: hold the left cable in your right hand and vice versa, at shoulder height.
v.l.un: One arm: helps you feel the muscle better.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

facepull.p: Cable at face height, rope held by the ends with thumbs pointing back. Step back with straight arms, torso braced.
s: Pull the rope toward your face, spreading your hands apart.
Drive your elbows out and back at shoulder height.
At the end, rotate your arms back, like a double-biceps pose.
Return slowly.
facepull.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
facepull.a: 1-second pause at the end, 2 seconds back.
facepull.f: Back of the shoulder, middle of the back and the muscles that rotate the shoulder outward.
d: Great for posture and shoulder health.
Pull the rope ends apart at the end, bringing your hands beside your ears.
e: Pulling with your body by leaning back.
facepull.c: Moderate load: the focus is the shoulder rotation at the end.

v.e.el: Band: anchor it to a door or post at face height.
v.p.se: Seated: removes body momentum; set the cable at eye level.

rotext.p: Stand side-on to a cable at elbow height, outer arm's elbow against your side and bent to 90°, hand in front of your belly. A towel between elbow and body helps.
s: Rotate your forearm outward, moving your hand away from your belly.
Keep your elbow against your side the whole time.
Go as far as is comfortable, about 45° out.
Return slowly.
rotext.r: Breathe out as you rotate and in as you return.
rotext.f: Back of the shoulder, deep inside (rotator cuff).
d: Very light load; 12 to 20 reps.
Great as a warm-up before chest and shoulder training.
e: Letting the elbow drift away from the body.
rotext.c: If you have strong shoulder pain, see a physical therapist.

v.e.el: Band: anchor it at elbow height.
v.e.ha: Dumbbell: do it lying on your side (on the non-working arm), rotating the dumbbell up.
v.p.ld: Lying on your side: elbow resting on your side, rotate the dumbbell up.
v.p.90: Arm at 90°: elbow at shoulder height, rotate your forearm up, like a surrender gesture.

cuban.p: Standing, light dumbbells in front of your thighs, overhand grip.
s: Do an upright row until your elbows are at shoulder height, forearms pointing down.
Rotate your forearms up, without dropping your elbows, until your hands are above your elbows.
Press the weights up as in a shoulder press.
Return the same way.
cuban.r: Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.
cuban.f: Shoulders, especially the back and the external rotators.
d: Very light load.
Do it slowly, without rushing.
e: Dropping the elbows during the rotation.
cuban.c: Stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.

v.e.bw: EZ bar: shoulder-width grip; requires good mobility.

rosca.p: Standing, feet hip-width apart, holding the load with straight arms at your sides, elbows against your sides, abs braced.
s: Bend your elbows and curl the load toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows still at your sides.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without bringing your elbows forward.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost fully straight.
rosca.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
rosca.a: Up in 1–2 s, down in 2–3 s. Straighten your arms at the bottom.
rosca.f: Biceps, with help from the forearm.
d: If you need to swing, the load is too heavy.
Leaning your back against a wall helps you avoid cheating.
e: Not straightening your arms at the bottom.
rosca.c: If your wrists hurt with a straight bar, use an EZ bar or dumbbells.

v.g.ne: Hammer (palms in): works more brachialis and forearm.
v.g.pr: Reverse (palms down): works more forearm; use less load.
v.e.bw: EZ bar: more comfortable for the wrists.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: you can rotate your palm up as you lift.
v.e.po: Cable: constant tension; stand close to the pulley.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: slightly more of the short head of the biceps.
v.w.fe: Close grip: slightly more of the long head.
v.p.cz: Across the body: bring the dumbbell toward the opposite shoulder; more brachialis.
v.l.al: Alternating: lift one arm at a time without twisting your torso.
v.l.un: One arm: hold onto a support with the other hand.

scott.p: Seated at the preacher bench, armpits snug over the top of the pad, arms resting on it, holding the bar with arms almost straight.
s: Bend your elbows and curl the bar toward your shoulders.
Keep the backs of your arms on the pad.
Stop before your forearm is vertical, where tension disappears.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
scott.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
scott.a: Slow lowering, 3 seconds, especially at the end.
scott.f: Biceps, very strong at the bottom of the movement.
d: The bottom part is the most important: control it well.
Adjust the seat height so your armpits are well supported.
e: Dropping the weight at the bottom and snapping the elbow straight.
Lifting your hips off the seat.
Taking your arms off the pad.
scott.c: Don't snap your elbow straight: that's where it's most vulnerable.

v.e.ha: Dumbbell: one arm at a time.
v.e.ma: Machine: line your elbow up with the machine's pivot.
v.e.po: Cable: constant tension; place the bench facing a low pulley.
v.l.un: One arm: better for concentration.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

rinclinada.p: Seated on a bench inclined at 45–60°, back and head supported, arms hanging behind your body, dumbbells with palms forward.
s: Curl the dumbbells up by bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows pointing down, without bringing them forward.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight, feeling the biceps stretch.
rinclinada.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
rinclinada.f: Biceps, mainly the long head, with the muscle well stretched.
d: Use less load than for standing curls.
Great for biceps growth, because it works the muscle in a stretched position.
e: Lifting your back off the bench.
rinclinada.c: If you feel the front of your shoulder, raise the bench a little.

v.e.po: Cable facing away (Bayesian): stand with your back to a low pulley, arm behind your body, and curl without bringing the elbow forward.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.
v.l.un: One arm: focus on each side.

concentrada.p: Seated, legs apart, torso leaning forward. Working arm's elbow resting on the inside of your thigh, arm straight down.
s: Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Keep your elbow still on your thigh.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, turning your pinky slightly up.
Lower slowly until straight.
concentrada.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
concentrada.a: Slow, with a pause at the top.
d: Great for feeling the muscle.
Use a moderate load and controlled reps.
e: Taking the elbow off the thigh.

v.e.po: Cable: kneeling or seated beside a low pulley; constant tension.

spider.p: Lie face down on an incline bench, chest supported, arms hanging straight down, holding the load.
s: Bend your elbows and curl the load up.
Keep your upper arms still and vertical.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower slowly until straight.
spider.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
spider.a: Pause at the top and lower in 2–3 s.
spider.f: Biceps, with peak tension at the top.
d: You can't cheat with your body, so use less load.
e: Lifting your chest off the bench.

v.e.bw: EZ bar: more comfortable for the wrists than a straight bar.

roscaalta.p: Stand between two high pulleys, holding each handle with arms open at shoulder height, palms up.
s: Bend your elbows and bring your hands toward your ears.
Keep your elbows still at shoulder height.
Squeeze your biceps at the end.
Return slowly.
roscaalta.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
roscaalta.a: Controlled, with a pause at the end.
d: Moderate load; it's a finishing exercise.

v.l.un: One arm: stand side-on to the pulley.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

drag.p: Standing, bar in front of your thighs, shoulder-width grip, palms forward.
s: Curl the bar up, dragging it along your body as your elbows move back.
Your elbows go behind your body, not forward.
Lift until the bar is near your chest.
Lower along the same path.
drag.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
drag.a: Controlled, 2 seconds on the way down.
d: Think about dragging the bar up your body.
e: Letting the bar drift away from your body.

v.e.bw: EZ bar: more comfortable for the wrists.

r21.p: Standing, as in a biceps curl, holding the load with straight arms.
s: 7 reps in the bottom half: from full extension to the elbow at 90°.
7 reps in the top half: from 90° to the top.
7 full reps.
All in a row, no rest.
r21.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
d: Use much less load than for a regular curl.
Good for varying your training.
e: Swinging your body on the last reps.

v.e.bw: EZ bar: more comfortable for the wrists.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: you can do both arms together.

zottman.p: Standing, dumbbells at your sides, palms forward, elbows against your sides.
s: Curl the dumbbells up with palms up, as in a regular curl.
At the top, turn your hands so the palms face down.
Lower slowly with palms down.
At the bottom, turn back to palms forward.
zottman.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
zottman.f: Biceps on the way up; forearm and brachialis on the way down.
d: Use a load you can lower slowly with your palms down.

pushdown.p: Standing, facing a high pulley, feet hip-width apart, torso leaning slightly forward. Elbows against your sides and bent, handle at chest height.
s: Push the handle down by straightening your elbows.
Keep your elbows still at your sides.
Straighten your arms fully and squeeze your triceps.
Return slowly until your forearms pass slightly above horizontal.
pushdown.r: Breathe out as you push and in as you return.
pushdown.a: 2 seconds back up; straighten fully at the bottom.
d: Think about moving only your forearm, like a hinge.
Keep your wrists straight.
e: Using your body weight by leaning far forward.
Letting the elbows rise and drift forward on the way back.
pushdown.c: No elbow pain allowed: if it hurts, change the attachment.

v.g.ba: Bar (palms down): lets you use more load.
v.g.co: Rope: at the bottom, pull the rope ends apart.
v.g.su: Underhand bar (palms up): use less load; focuses the inner part of the triceps.
v.l.un: One arm: with a single handle, palm up or down.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

frances.p: Standing or seated, back to the pulley (or holding the weight), arms overhead, elbows pointing forward or up, close to your head.
s: Bend your elbows and lower the load behind your head.
Keep your elbows still and pointing forward.
Lower until you feel the triceps well stretched.
Straighten your arms back overhead.
frances.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift.
frances.a: Lower in 2–3 s, no bouncing at the bottom.
frances.f: Triceps, especially the long head, which is stretched in this position.
d: Training the triceps in a stretched position seems to help it grow more.
Keep your abs braced so your back doesn't arch.
frances.c: If your elbow hurts, reduce the load or the range.

v.e.po: Cable: back to the pulley, rope behind your head, one foot forward for balance.
v.e.ha: Dumbbell: hold one dumbbell with both hands by the top plate.
v.e.bw: EZ bar: close grip, elbows forward.
v.p.se: Seated with back support: protects the lower back.
v.l.un: One arm: hold your elbow with the other hand to guide it.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

testa.p: Lying on a bench, holding the bar with straight arms over your chest, shoulder-width grip.
s: Tilt your arms slightly back toward your head.
Bend your elbows and lower the bar to your forehead or behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling, without flaring.
Straighten your arms back up.
testa.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift.
d: Lowering behind your head stretches the triceps more.
Use a spotter with heavy loads.
e: Moving the shoulders along with it.
testa.c: Always control the descent: the bar passes close to your face.

v.e.ba: Straight bar: may bother the wrists; try the EZ bar.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: palms facing each other; lower beside your head.
v.e.po: Cable: bench facing a low pulley; constant tension.
v.b.in: Incline bench: the triceps is more stretched.
v.b.de: Decline bench: shorter range; good for heavier loads.

coice.p: Place one hand and one knee on a bench, torso parallel to the floor, back straight. The other arm holds the dumbbell with the elbow bent to 90° and close to your body.
s: Straighten your elbow, moving the dumbbell back.
Keep your upper arm still, parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your triceps with your arm straight.
Return slowly to 90°.
coice.r: Breathe out as you extend and in as you return.
d: Light load: tension is highest with the arm straight.
Raise your elbow slightly above your torso for more range.

v.e.po: Cable: tension from the start; cable from a low pulley.
v.l.bi: Both arms: torso bent forward, unsupported, back straight.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.
v.l.un: One arm: supported on the bench, as described above.

jm.p: Lying on the bench as for a close-grip bench press (shoulder-width), bar over your chest.
s: Lower the bar by bending your elbows and letting them move slightly forward.
The bar comes down toward your chin or upper chest.
Stop with the bar a few centimeters from your face.
Press back up by straightening your arms.
jm.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift.
jm.a: Controlled; it's a mix between a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher.
d: Start light until you get the hang of it.
Use a spotter.
jm.c: A technical exercise: learn it with light loads.

v.e.sm: Smith: the track helps control the path.

tmaq.p: Seated in the machine, back supported, elbows lined up with the machine's pivot, holding the handles.
s: Push the handles by straightening your elbows.
Keep your elbows still.
Straighten fully and squeeze your triceps.
Return slowly.
tmaq.r: Breathe out as you push and in as you return.
d: Set the seat so your elbow is at the height of the pivot.
e: Lifting your back off the pad.

punho.p: Seated, forearms resting on your thighs or a bench, wrists past the edge, holding the load.
s: Let the load go down, bending your wrist downward.
Lift the load by bending only your wrist, without moving your forearm.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly.
d: You can let the bar roll down to your fingertips for more range (palms up).
e: Too much load and a short range.

v.g.pr: Palms down: works the top of the forearm; use much less load.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: one arm at a time.
v.e.po: Low cable: constant tension.
v.p.ct: Bar behind the back: standing, holding the bar behind you, palms back; lift by bending your wrists.

farmer.p: Standing, a heavy load in each hand at your sides, shoulders back and down, chest open, abs braced.
s: Pick the loads up from the floor by squatting with a straight back.
Walk with short, firm steps.
Keep your body upright, without leaning to the sides.
Walk for the planned distance or time and squat to put the loads down.
farmer.r: Breathe in short, steady breaths without relaxing your abs.
farmer.f: Forearms (grip), traps, abs and glute medius.
d: Great for grip and posture.
Look ahead, not at your feet.
e: Picking up the load with a rounded back.

v.e.kb: Kettlebell: hold by the handle, arm straight at your side.
v.e.hx: Trap bar: more load; lift it like a deadlift.
v.l.un: One side (suitcase): load on one side only; your abs work to keep you from leaning.

hang.p: Grip the pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width apart and hang, arms straight, feet off the floor.
s: Hang with straight arms.
Keep your shoulders slightly active, without letting your head sink between them.
Breathe and hold for the planned time.
Get down carefully.
hang.f: Forearms and hands; stretches the back.
d: Great for improving grip.
Can help decompress the spine after leg training.
e: Dropping off all at once at the end.

v.l.un: One hand: much harder; keep the other hand close by if needed.

roller.p: Standing, arms straight in front at shoulder height, holding the wrist roller with the weight hanging from the cord.
s: Turn the roller one wrist at a time, winding the cord up.
Raise until the weight reaches the roller.
Unwind slowly, turning the other way.
Keep your arms straight in front.
roller.a: Slow on the way up and down.
d: Roll forward and backward in different sets.
e: Letting the weight fall all at once.

encolh.p: Standing, holding the load with straight arms, feet hip-width apart.
s: Lift your shoulders toward your ears without bending your elbows.
Hold for 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly until your shoulders are well down.
Keep your neck straight.
encolh.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
encolh.a: Pause at the top and lower slowly.
d: Lift straight up, slightly back.
Wrist straps help when your grip tires first.
encolh.c: Don't roll your shoulders in circles under load.

v.e.ha: Dumbbells: at your sides, more range.
v.e.hx: Trap bar: hands at your sides.
v.e.sm: Smith: the track guides you; full focus on the traps.
v.e.ma: Machine: adjust the height so you start with shoulders down.
v.e.po: Cable: constant tension.

terra.p: Feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot. Hinge at the hips, bend your knees and grip the bar just outside your legs. Back straight, chest forward, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, arms straight.
s: Take the slack out: pull lightly on the bar until it presses against the plates and your body is tight.
Push the floor away with your feet, raising hips and shoulders together.
Keep the bar dragging up your legs.
Finish standing tall with glutes squeezed, without leaning back.
Lower by pushing your hips back and, once the bar passes your knees, bending your knees.
terra.r: Breathe in and brace your abs before each rep; breathe out at the top or back on the floor, before the next one.
terra.a: Firm lift; controlled lowering, without dropping the bar.
terra.f: Glutes, hamstrings and lower back; back, traps and forearms hold the bar.
d: Think about pushing the floor away, not pulling the bar.
Start each rep from a dead stop on the floor.
e: Letting the bar drift away from your body.
Raising the hips before the shoulders.
Hyperextending the back at the top.
terra.c: Learn it with light loads. Stop if your lower back rounds.

v.st.su: Sumo: feet wide, toes out, hands inside your legs, torso more upright; more adductors and quads.
v.e.hx: Trap bar: stand inside the bar, neutral grip; easier to keep a straight back and more quads.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: dumbbells beside or in front of your legs; good for learning the movement.

stiff.p: Standing, feet hip-width apart, bar in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent and fixed.
s: Push your hips back, tilting your torso with a straight back.
Let the bar slide down your thighs.
Lower until you feel your hamstrings stretch well, usually just below the knees.
Come back up by driving your hips forward.
stiff.r: Breathe in and brace your abs before lowering; breathe out as you finish the lift.
d: Think about closing a door with your butt.
The descent ends where you can still keep your back straight.
e: Rounding your back to go lower.
Bending your knees and turning it into a deadlift.
Letting the bar drift away from your body.
stiff.c: Stop the descent before your lower back rounds.

v.e.ha: Dumbbells: slide them down the front of your legs.
v.e.sm: Smith: the track guides you; place your feet so the bar passes close to your legs.
v.e.kb: Kettlebell: hold the handle with both hands.
v.l.un: Single leg: the back leg rises as your torso lowers; hips square, lean on a wall if needed.

bomdia.p: Standing, bar on your back as in a squat, feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent.
s: Push your hips back, tilting your torso with a straight back.
Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, or as far as you can keep your back straight.
Keep the bar tight on your back.
Come back up by driving your hips forward.
bomdia.r: Breathe in and brace your abs before lowering; breathe out as you come up.
d: Start with a very light load.
It's similar to the Romanian deadlift, but with the load on your back.
bomdia.c: A technical exercise: increase the load slowly.

v.e.el: Band: stand on the band and loop it behind your neck; great for learning.

remcurv.p: Standing, holding the bar, knees slightly bent. Tilt your torso forward with a straight back, 30–45° above the floor, arms hanging straight down.
s: Pull the bar toward your belly, near the navel.
Drive your elbows back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Squeeze your back at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
remcurv.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower, keeping your abs braced.
remcurv.a: Short pause at the top, 2 seconds down.
remcurv.f: Back (lats, middle of the back), back of the shoulder and biceps.
d: Don't let your torso rise on each rep.
Think about pulling with your elbows, not your hands.
remcurv.c: Keep your lower back straight the whole time; if it tires, end the set.

v.e.ha: Dumbbells: palms in, elbows close to the body.
v.e.sm: Smith: the track guides you; keep the same torso angle.
v.e.tb: T-bar: stand over the bar and pull the handles to your chest.
v.g.su: Underhand grip (palms up): more biceps and lower lats; pull to your lower belly.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: elbows wider, more middle back and rear delts.
v.w.fe: Close grip: elbows close to the body, more lats.

rembaixa.p: Seated at the low row, feet supported, knees slightly bent, torso straight, arms straight in front holding the handle.
s: Pull the handle toward your belly.
Drive your elbows back, close to your body, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Squeeze your back at the end.
Return by straightening your arms and letting your shoulders move forward a little.
rembaixa.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
rembaixa.a: Controlled return in 2 seconds; stretch your back well at the front.
rembaixa.f: Back (lats and middle of the back) and biceps.
d: Letting your shoulder blades move forward on the return increases the range.
Your torso can lean a little, but without swinging.

v.e.ma: Machine: chest against the pad, no swinging.
v.g.pr: Overhand grip (palms down): elbows wider, more middle back.
v.g.su: Underhand grip (palms up): more biceps and lower lats.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: elbows out, more middle back and rear delts.
v.w.fe: Close grip (V-handle): elbows close to the body, more lats.
v.l.un: One arm: you can rotate your torso slightly for a bigger stretch.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

remapoiada.p: Chest against the machine's pad or an incline bench, feet planted, arms straight holding the handles.
s: Pull the handles, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Keep your chest on the pad.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
remapoiada.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
remapoiada.a: Pause at the end and 2 seconds back.
remapoiada.f: Middle of the back, lats and back of the shoulder.
d: Great for anyone who feels their lower back in the bent-over row.
With the torso supported, you can focus only on your back.
e: Lifting your chest off the pad to pull.

v.c.ab: Elbows out to the sides: more middle back and rear delts.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells on an incline bench: lie face down and row both dumbbells.
v.e.ba: Barbell or supported T-bar: chest on the pad, grab the bar below.
v.l.un: One arm: focus on each side.
v.l.al: Alternating: one arm at a time.

serrote.p: Place the hand and knee of the same side on a bench, back straight and parallel to the floor. The other hand holds the dumbbell with a straight arm, that side's foot on the floor.
s: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip.
Drive your elbow back, close to your body.
Squeeze your back at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight, letting your shoulder drop a little.
serrote.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.
serrote.a: Pause at the top and 2 seconds down.
d: Think about bringing your elbow toward your back pocket.
You can use a lot of load with your spine protected.

v.e.po: Low cable: standing with your torso bent, one arm at a time.
v.e.lm: Landmine (Meadows row): side-on to the end of the bar, grip the end overhand and pull.

reminv.p: Lie under a bar fixed in a rack or Smith machine at waist height. Grip it with straight arms, body straight from heels to shoulders.
s: Pull your chest toward the bar.
Keep your body straight, like a plank.
Touch the bar with your chest or get close.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
reminv.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.
reminv.f: Back, back of the shoulder and biceps.
d: The more horizontal your body, the harder it is.
A great step toward pull-ups.

v.e.tr: Rings or TRX: your hands can rotate freely; demands more stability.

barrafixa.p: Hang from the bar with hands slightly wider than your shoulders, arms straight, legs together or crossed, abs braced.
s: Start by pulling your shoulders down, without bending your arms.
Pull your body up, driving your elbows down and back.
Rise until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
barrafixa.r: Breathe out as you go up and in as you lower.
barrafixa.f: Lats, with biceps and middle back helping.
d: Think about pulling your elbows toward your pockets.
If you can't do one yet, do slow negatives only or use a band.
e: Letting your shoulders rise to your ears.
barrafixa.c: Lower under control; dropping all at once stresses the shoulders.

v.g.su: Underhand grip (chin-up, palms toward you): more biceps; usually easier.
v.g.ne: Neutral grip (palms in): comfortable for shoulders and elbows.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: shorter range and harder.
v.w.fe: Close grip: more range and more biceps.
v.e.ma: Assisted (machine): the counterweight helps; reduce it gradually.
v.e.lt: Weighted: use a dip belt or a dumbbell between your feet, only after you can do 8–10 bodyweight reps.

puxada.p: Seated at the machine, thighs locked under the pad, holding the bar with straight arms, torso leaning slightly back.
s: Pull the bar toward your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your back with the bar near your chest.
Return slowly until your arms are fully straight.
puxada.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
d: Let your arms straighten fully at the top to stretch your back.
No need to lean back much.
puxada.c: Always pull in front of your body, never behind the neck.

v.g.su: Underhand grip: more biceps and lower lats.
v.g.ne: Neutral grip (V-handle or parallel bar): comfortable and good for load.
v.w.ab: Wide grip: slightly more upper lats.
v.e.ma: Plate-loaded machine: each arm moves independently.
v.l.un: One arm: with a single handle, rotate your torso slightly to stretch more.

escap.p: Hang from the pull-up bar with straight arms and relaxed shoulders, close to your ears.
s: Without bending your arms, pull your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Your body rises a few centimeters.
Hold for 1–2 seconds.
Slowly return to the relaxed position.
escap.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
d: Great for learning to engage your back before pull-ups.

pullover.p: Standing facing a high pulley, holding the rope or bar with straight arms in front, torso leaning slightly forward.
s: With arms almost straight, pull the handle in an arc down to your thighs.
Keep your elbows fixed.
Squeeze your back at the bottom.
Return slowly until your arms are overhead, feeling your back stretch.
pullover.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
pullover.f: Lats; a little chest and triceps.
d: Great for feeling your lats without using your biceps.
e: Bending the elbows and turning it into a triceps exercise.

v.e.ha: Lying dumbbell: on a bench, hold one dumbbell over your chest and lower it behind your head with arms almost straight until you feel the stretch; come back.
v.e.ma: Machine: back supported, elbows on the pads.

extlombar.p: On the 45° back extension bench, hips on the edge of the pad, feet locked in, body straight, arms crossed over your chest.
s: Lower your torso by hinging at the hips, back straight.
Go down until you feel your hamstrings stretch.
Come up until your body is in a straight line.
Don't go past straight.
extlombar.r: Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
d: Rounding the back slightly focuses the lower back; a straight back focuses the glutes.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
e: Going past the line of the body, over-arching.
extlombar.c: Start without weight; add it gradually.

v.p.90: Roman chair (90°): torso parallel to the floor; bigger range and harder.
v.p.ch: On the floor (superman): lying face down, raise arms and legs together, hold and lower.
v.e.an: Plate on chest: hug the plate against your chest.

birddog.p: On all fours, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips, back flat like a table, abs braced.
s: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back at the same time.
Bring the arm and leg in line with your body.
Hold for 2–3 seconds without moving your hips.
Return and switch sides.
birddog.r: Breathe out as you extend and in as you return.
birddog.a: Slow, with a pause on each rep.
d: Imagine a glass of water on your back that can't spill.
Great as a warm-up and for people with back pain.
e: Lifting the leg above the line of the body.

socoserr.p: Lying on your back on a bench, holding a dumbbell with your arm straight over your shoulder.
s: Without bending your elbow, push the dumbbell toward the ceiling.
Your shoulder comes off the bench a few centimeters (the shoulder blade moves forward).
Hold for 1 second.
Lower slowly, letting your shoulder touch the bench.
socoserr.r: Breathe out as you push and in as you return.
socoserr.f: Serratus (side of the ribs, under the armpit).
d: It's a small movement: only the shoulder moves.
Helps shoulder health and stability.

v.e.po: Standing cable: back to the pulley, punch the cable forward, straightening your arm and moving your shoulder forward at the end.

scaption.p: Standing, light dumbbells at your sides, thumbs up.
s: Raise your straight arms at about 30° in front of your body (between front and side).
Keep raising overhead, past 120°.
At the top, let your shoulder blades rotate upward naturally.
Lower slowly.
scaption.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
d: Very light load.
Good for improving how your shoulder moves.
e: Arching the lower back to go higher.

pushplus.p: In a push-up position (or on your knees), arms straight, body straight.
s: Do a regular push-up.
As you straighten your arms, push the floor a bit further, moving your upper back away from the floor.
Your shoulder blades spread and your upper back rounds slightly.
Return and repeat.
pushplus.r: Breathe out as you push and in as you lower.
d: You can also do only the extra push, without bending your arms.

prancprot.p: In a plank on your forearms or hands, body straight, abs braced.
s: Push the floor away, moving your upper back away from the floor and spreading your shoulder blades.
Hold the position.
Let your shoulder blades come back slowly.
Repeat or hold still.
prancprot.a: Slow reps or sets of 20–40 seconds.
d: Keep your hips in line.
e: Letting the hips rise or sag.

wallslide.p: Facing a wall, forearms resting on a foam roller against the wall at chest height.
s: Press lightly into the wall with your forearms.
Roll the roller up, bringing your arms overhead.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Come down slowly.
wallslide.r: Breathe out as you go up and in as you come down.
d: A great warm-up for shoulder and back workouts.

crunch.p: Lying on your back, knees bent, feet on the floor, hands on your chest or behind your head without pulling your neck.
s: Curl your torso up, bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Lift only your shoulder blades off the floor; your lower back stays down.
Squeeze your abs at the top.
Lower slowly.
crunch.r: Breathe all the air out as you curl up and in as you lower.
crunch.a: Controlled, with a pause at the top.
d: Think about curling your spine, not lifting your whole torso.
Look at the ceiling or your knees, with your chin slightly off your chest.
e: Pulling your head with your hands.
Lifting your whole torso from the hips (it becomes a hip flexor exercise).
crunch.c: If your neck hurts, rest your head in your hands without pulling.

v.e.bo: Stability ball: lower back on the ball; let your abs stretch back before curling up.
v.e.po: Kneeling cable: hold the rope by your head and curl your torso down, without sitting back on your heels.
v.e.ma: Machine: adjust it so you bend at your abs.
v.e.dc: Decline bench: harder; feet locked in.
v.v.br: Arms straight: reach for your knees with your hands.
v.v.pv: Legs vertical: legs up, curl your torso toward your feet.
v.v.ca: Pushing your heels into the floor: reduces the use of the hip flexors.

bicicleta.p: Lying on your back, hands behind your head without pulling, legs raised with knees at 90°.
s: Bring your right elbow toward your left knee, rotating your torso.
At the same time, straighten your right leg out in front.
Switch sides: left elbow toward right knee.
Keep alternating.
bicicleta.f: Abs and obliques (sides of the belly).
d: Rotate with your torso, not just your elbow.
e: Letting the lower back lift off the floor.

reverso.p: Lying on your back, arms at your sides, legs up with knees bent.
s: Curl your hips up, lifting your butt off the floor and bringing your knees toward your chest.
Use your abs, not leg momentum.
Hold for 1 second at the top.
Lower slowly.
reverso.r: Breathe out as your hips lift and in as you lower.
reverso.a: Slow, especially on the way down.
d: Think about curling your spine from the bottom up.

v.e.dc: Decline bench: hold the bench behind your head; it gets harder.

elevpernas.p: Hanging from the pull-up bar, arms straight, shoulders engaged, body still.
s: Raise your legs in front without swinging.
At the end, curl your hips forward, bringing your pelvis toward your chest.
Hold for a moment.
Lower slowly, without swinging.
elevpernas.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
elevpernas.f: Abs and the muscles at the front of the hip.
d: The most important part is curling the hips at the end, not just lifting the legs.
Grip straps help if your hands tire.
e: Lifting only the legs without curling the hips.
Dropping the legs on the way down.

v.e.ca: Captain's chair: back against the pad, forearms supported; more stable.
v.e.ch: Lying on the floor: hands at your sides or under your hips, lower back pressed into the floor.

dragon.p: Lying on your back on a bench, holding the bench behind your head with your hands.
s: Raise your whole body, resting only on your shoulders and upper back.
Keep your body straight like a plank, from shoulders to feet.
Lower your body slowly without bending at the hips.
Stop before touching and come back up.
dragon.r: Breathe out as you lower and in as you rise.
dragon.a: Very slow on the way down.
d: An advanced exercise.
Start with knees bent or with the lowering phase only.
e: Putting the weight on your neck.
dragon.c: Requires strong abs; don't strain your neck.

tesoura.p: Lying on your back, hands at your sides or under your hips, legs straight and slightly off the floor.
s: Raise one leg and lower the other, alternating.
Short, quick movements, like kicking in water.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Continue for the planned time.
tesoura.f: Abs, more the lower part, and front of the hip.
d: The closer your legs are to the floor, the harder it is.
e: Letting the lower back lift off the floor.

prancha.p: Rest on your forearms with elbows under your shoulders and on the balls of your feet. Body straight from head to heels.
s: Squeeze your abs and glutes.
Keep your hips in line with your body, neither high nor low.
Look at the floor, neck straight.
Hold for the planned time.
prancha.r: Breathe normally, in short steady breaths.
prancha.a: 20–60 seconds; several good sets beat one long, sloppy one.
d: Pull your elbows toward your feet (without moving them) to make it stronger.
When it gets easy, lift one arm or one leg.

v.v.ma: On your hands (arms straight): slightly easier for the abs and works the shoulders more.

pranchalat.p: Lying on your side, resting on your forearm with the elbow under your shoulder, legs straight and feet stacked.
s: Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Keep your hips facing forward, without rotating.
Hold for the planned time.
Switch sides.
pranchalat.f: Sides of the belly (obliques) and side of the hip.
d: Easier: rest on your bottom knee.
e: Rotating the body forward or back.

v.v.ab: With abduction: raise and lower your top leg, working the glute medius more.

lenhador.p: Standing side-on to a high pulley, feet apart, holding the handle with both hands above the shoulder closest to the pulley.
s: Pull the handle diagonally down across your body to the outside of the opposite knee.
Rotate your torso and feet together, like chopping wood.
Keep your arms almost straight.
Return slowly.
lenhador.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
d: The movement comes from your torso, not your arms.

v.e.el: Band: anchored high on a post or door.
v.e.ha: Dumbbell: hold it with both hands and do the same diagonal movement.
v.v.bc: Low to high: low pulley; bring the handle from the knee to above the opposite shoulder.

pallof.p: Standing side-on to a cable at chest height, holding the handle with both hands near your chest, feet hip-width apart, abs braced.
s: Press the handle forward until your arms are straight.
Don't let your body rotate toward the pulley.
Hold for 2–3 seconds.
Bring the handle back to your chest.
pallof.f: Abs and obliques, which work to stop your body from rotating.
d: The farther from the pulley, the harder it is.

twist.p: Seated on the floor, knees bent, torso leaning back about 45°, back straight, holding the load in front of your chest.
s: Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the load beside your hip.
Return to the center.
Rotate to the other side.
Keep alternating.
twist.a: Controlled; it's not meant to be fast.
d: To make it harder, lift your feet off the floor.
e: Moving only the arms without rotating the torso.
twist.c: If your lower back bothers you, keep your feet on the floor and reduce the load.

v.e.co: No weight: hands together in front of your chest.
v.e.bo: Medicine ball: hold it with both hands.

wiper.p: Hanging from the pull-up bar (or lying on the floor holding something behind your head), legs up, close to vertical.
s: With your legs up, rotate them to one side, like a windshield wiper.
Return to the center.
Rotate to the other side.
Control the whole movement.
wiper.r: Breathe out as your legs go to the side and in as they return.
d: An advanced exercise. It's easier on the floor.

sidebend.p: Standing, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, the other hand on your waist.
s: Bend your torso toward the dumbbell side, lowering slowly.
Come back up, leaning a little to the other side.
Keep your torso facing forward, without rotating.
Do all the reps and switch sides.
sidebend.r: Breathe out as you come up and in as you lower.
sidebend.f: Oblique on the side opposite the dumbbell.
d: Don't hold two dumbbells: one balances the other and removes the work.

v.e.po: Cable: side-on to a low pulley; constant tension.

roda.p: Kneeling on the floor (use a mat), holding the wheel under your shoulders, arms straight, abs braced.
s: Roll the wheel forward, extending your body.
Keep your abs braced and your lower back from sagging.
Go as far as you can without losing your posture.
Come back by pulling with your abs.
roda.r: Breathe in as you roll out and out as you come back.
d: Start by rolling toward a wall, which acts as a limit.
e: Going too far at the beginning.
Raising the hips before the torso.
roda.c: If your lower back hurts, shorten the distance.

v.p.pe: Standing: very advanced; only after mastering the kneeling version.
v.e.ba: Barbell with plates: same movement, with the bar rolling.

hipthrust.p: Sit on the floor with your upper back (just below the shoulder blades) against the edge of a bench. Barbell over your hips with a pad. Feet on the floor hip-width apart, knees bent.
s: Push through your heels and raise your hips.
Rise until your torso and thighs are in line, with your shins vertical.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, chin slightly tucked.
Lower slowly.
hipthrust.r: Breathe in at the bottom, brace your abs and breathe out at the top.
d: Keep your ribs down: the movement comes from your hips, not your lower back.
Adjust your feet: if you feel it in your quads, move your feet farther out; if in your hamstrings, bring them closer.
e: Arching the lower back at the top.
hipthrust.c: Use a pad on the bar so it doesn't hurt your hips.

v.ap.ch: On the floor (glute bridge): back on the floor; shorter range, easier to set up.
v.e.ma: Machine: set the back pad at shoulder-blade height.
v.e.sm: Smith: the track guides you; set up the bench first.
v.e.ha: Dumbbell: rest it on your hips and hold it with your hands.
v.e.co: Bodyweight: good for learning or for high reps.
v.l.un: Single leg: the other leg stays bent in the air; keep your hips level.

coicegl.p: Standing facing a low pulley, ankle strap on your ankle, hands on the machine, torso leaning slightly.
s: Move your straight leg back.
Keep your lower back straight: the movement is only from the hip.
Squeeze your glute at the end.
Return slowly.
coicegl.r: Breathe out as your leg goes back and in as it returns.
coicegl.a: Pause at the end, 2 seconds back.
d: Lean your torso forward a little for more range.
e: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher.

v.e.ma: Glute machine: chest on the pad, push the platform back.
v.e.4w: 4-way hip machine: roller behind the thigh, push back.
v.e.co: All fours: on the floor, move your leg back and up.
v.e.cn: Ankle weight: on all fours or standing.
v.j.fl: Knee bent: push the sole of your foot toward the ceiling; more glutes and less hamstrings.

swing.p: Feet slightly wider than your shoulders, kettlebell on the floor in front. Hinge at the hips, back straight, and grab the handle with both hands.
s: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs, like a football snap.
Drive your hips forward hard, sending the weight up to chest height.
Your arms only guide it: the power comes from your hips.
Let the weight come down and push your hips back again.
swing.r: Breathe out forcefully on each hip drive.
d: It's a hip hinge, not a squat.
Squeeze your glutes and abs at the top, like a standing plank.
e: Squatting instead of hinging at the hips.
swing.c: Keep the space in front of and behind you clear.

v.e.ha: Dumbbell: hold it by one end.

abducao.p: Seated on the abduction machine, back supported, pads on the outside of your knees.
s: Spread your legs apart.
Open as far as you can with control.
Hold for 1 second.
Return slowly without slamming the weight.
abducao.r: Breathe out as you open and in as you return.
d: Moderate to high reps work well.
e: Slamming the weight on the way back.

v.e.po: Cable: ankle strap on the outer ankle, move your leg out to the side.
v.e.co: Lying on your side: raise your top leg straight, slightly back.
v.p.fr: Torso leaning forward: works the glute max more.

lateralwalk.p: Band above your knees or around your ankles, knees slightly bent, hips slightly back, feet hip-width apart.
s: Take a wide step to the side.
Bring the other foot over without letting the band go slack.
Keep your knees pointing forward.
Walk one way and come back.
d: Great as a warm-up before leg training.

ostra.p: Lying on your side, band above your knees, knees bent at about 45°, feet together, head resting on your arm.
s: Keeping your feet together, open your top knee.
Don't let your hips roll back.
Hold for 1 second.
Close slowly.
ostra.r: Breathe out as you open and in as you close.
d: Put your top hand on your hip to feel whether it's rolling.

hidrante.p: On all fours, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips.
s: Keeping your knee bent at 90°, lift your leg out to the side.
Raise until your thigh is near hip height.
Hold for 1 second.
Lower slowly.
hidrante.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
d: A band above the knees makes it harder.
e: Leaning your torso to the other side.

joelhopolia.p: Standing with your back to a low pulley, ankle strap on, hand resting on something in front.
s: Raise your knee in front, bending at the hip.
Raise until your thigh passes horizontal.
Hold for 1 second.
Lower slowly.
joelhopolia.r: Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.
d: Keep your torso upright, without leaning back.

aducao.p: Seated on the adduction machine, back supported, pads on the inside of your knees, legs apart.
s: Squeeze your legs together, bringing your knees closer.
Squeeze your inner thighs at the end.
Return slowly, opening until you feel a stretch.
Don't slam the weight.
aducao.r: Breathe out as you close and in as you open.
d: Opening wide on the return works the adductors in a stretched position.

v.e.po: Cable: ankle strap on the inner ankle, bring your leg across in front of the other.
v.e.bo: Ball between the knees: lying or seated, squeeze the ball and hold.

copenhagen.p: Lying on your side, resting on your forearm. Place your top leg on a bench (at the knee for an easier version, or at the foot), bottom leg free.
s: Press your top leg into the bench and lift your hips.
Body in a straight line.
The bottom leg can rise to the bench or stay free.
Hold for the planned time and switch sides.
copenhagen.f: Inner thigh and sides of the belly.
d: Helps prevent groin injuries.
Supporting the knee instead of the foot is much easier.
copenhagen.c: Start with the knee supported and short holds.

agach.p: Bar resting on your traps (behind the neck, on the muscle), hands tight on the bar, feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly out, chest up.
s: Breathe in and brace your abs.
Lower by moving your hips back and down while bending your knees.
Your knees track in the direction of your toes and can go past them.
Go down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, back straight.
Stand up by pushing the floor with your whole foot, hips and shoulders rising together.
agach.r: Breathe in and brace your abs before lowering; breathe out once past the hard part of the lift or at the top.
agach.a: 2–3 seconds down. Going deeper (if your posture allows) works the glutes and thighs more.
agach.f: Quads (front of the thigh) and glutes.
d: Think about spreading the floor with your feet, pushing your knees slightly out.
Flat, stable shoes help; a heel wedge helps if your ankle mobility is limited.
e: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Raising the hips before the chest.
agach.c: Use the rack's safety pins with heavy loads.

v.e.bf: Front squat: bar resting on the front of your shoulders, elbows high; more upright torso and more quads.
v.e.ha: Dumbbell (goblet): hold the dumbbell against your chest; great for learning.
v.e.sm: Smith: feet slightly in front of your body; the track guides you.
v.e.ct: Belt squat: the load hangs from your hips and spares your back.
v.am.pr: Deep: go as low as you can with a straight back; more glutes and thighs working in a stretched position.
v.pe.su: Sumo: feet wide and toes out; more adductors and glutes.

hack.p: Back and shoulders against the machine, feet on the platform hip-width apart, toes slightly out.
s: Release the machine.
Lower by bending your knees, back pressed against the pad.
Go as low as you comfortably can.
Push the platform with your whole foot to stand up.
hack.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you push.
hack.a: 2–3 s down, no bouncing at the bottom.
d: Lets you go deep with your spine supported.
e: Lifting your hips off the pad.
Locking the knees hard at the top.

v.e.pd: Pendulum: the movement follows an arc; great for going deep.
v.pe.al: Feet high: more glutes and hamstrings.
v.pe.bx: Feet low: more quads; the knee travels further forward.

legpress.p: Seated in the machine, back and hips well supported, feet on the platform hip-width apart.
s: Release the machine with your legs almost straight.
Lower by bending your knees toward your chest.
Go down as far as your hips stay on the seat.
Push the platform with your whole foot, without locking your knees at the top.
legpress.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you push.
d: Your knees follow the direction of your toes.
If your hips lift off the seat at the bottom, go less deep.
e: Lifting the hips off the seat (the lower back rounds).
legpress.c: Never snap your knees back at the top with heavy loads.

v.e.ho: Horizontal (seated): the same, but pushing forward.
v.pe.al: Feet high: more glutes and hamstrings.
v.pe.ab: Feet wide: more adductors and glutes.
v.l.un: Single leg: reduce the load a lot.

sissy.p: Standing, holding a support with one hand, feet hip-width apart, up on your toes.
s: Bend your knees, pushing them forward while leaning your torso back.
Keep your hips extended: body straight from knees to shoulders.
Lower as far as is comfortable.
Come back up using your thighs.
sissy.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
d: Start with a short range.
sissy.c: Requires healthy knees; stop if it hurts.

v.e.ma: Machine or support: locks your feet and makes the movement easier and safer.

espanhol.p: Anchor a strong band to a fixed support at knee height. Loop it behind your knees and step back until the band is taut.
s: Lean your torso slightly back against the band.
Squat with a more upright torso, letting the band hold your knees.
Lower to about 90° at the knees.
Stand up by straightening your legs.
espanhol.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
espanhol.a: Slow or with holds at the bottom.
d: Widely used in knee rehab.
e: Bending too much at the hips.

afundo.p: Standing, feet hip-width apart, dumbbells at your sides, torso upright.
s: Step forward, far enough that both knees reach about 90° at the bottom.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Your front knee tracks over your toes.
Push the floor with your front foot to come back.
afundo.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
afundo.f: Glutes and thighs of the front leg.
d: Longer step and torso slightly forward: more glutes.
Shorter step and upright torso: more quads.
e: Step too short, with the heel lifting.
Banging the back knee on the floor.

v.dir.tr: Reverse: step back; usually easier on the knees.
v.dir.an: Walking: chain one step after another, moving forward.
v.dir.bu: Bulgarian: back foot on a bench; almost all the weight is on the front leg.
v.e.ba: Barbell: on your back as in a squat; requires balance.
v.e.sm: Smith: more stable; place your front foot well forward.

stepup.p: Facing a bench or box at knee height, dumbbells at your sides.
s: Place your whole foot on the bench.
Step up by pushing with the top leg, without pushing off with the bottom one.
Stand up tall on the bench.
Step down slowly with the same leg that went up first.
stepup.r: Breathe out as you step up and in as you step down.
stepup.f: Glutes and thigh of the top leg.
d: Lean your torso slightly forward for more glutes.
Higher bench = harder.
e: Pushing off with the bottom leg.

v.e.ba: Barbell on your back: requires balance; use a lower bench.

pistol.p: Standing on one leg, the other straight in front, arms forward for balance.
s: Lower by bending the standing leg, pushing your hips back.
Keep the other leg in front, off the floor.
Go as low as you can with control.
Stand up by pushing the floor.
pistol.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
d: Start by sitting on a bench and standing up on one leg.
Holding a support helps at first.

aflateral.p: Standing, feet together, dumbbells in front of or beside your body.
s: Take a wide step to the side.
Bend the stepping knee, pushing your hips back; the other leg stays straight.
Lower until you feel the inner thigh of the straight leg stretch.
Push the floor to come back.
aflateral.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you come back.
d: Both feet point forward.

v.v.co: Cossack: go very deep, almost sitting on your heel, with the toes of the straight leg pointing up.
v.e.co: Bodyweight: arms in front for balance.

extensora.p: Seated on the leg extension, back supported, knee lined up with the machine's pivot, pad in front of your ankle.
s: Straighten your legs, lifting the pad.
Extend fully and squeeze your thighs at the top.
Hold for 1 second.
Lower slowly until your knees are well bent.
extensora.r: Breathe out as you extend and in as you lower.
d: Hold the handles so your hips don't lift off the seat.
e: Lifting the hips off the seat.

v.p.rc: Reclined backrest: the rectus femoris is more stretched and works more.
v.l.un: Single leg: helps fix strength differences between legs.

flexora.p: Seated on the leg curl, knee lined up with the machine's pivot, pad behind your ankles, thigh pad locking your legs in.
s: Bend your knees, pulling the pad down and back.
Bend as far as you can.
Squeeze your hamstrings.
Return slowly until straight.
flexora.r: Breathe out as you bend and in as you return.
d: The seated version works the hamstrings in a more stretched position and seems to give better results.
Lean your torso slightly forward to stretch more.
e: Lifting the hips off the seat.

v.p.de: Lying (prone): face down, hips pressed into the bench.
v.p.pe: Standing: one leg at a time.
v.l.un: Single leg: good for fixing differences.

nordica.p: Kneeling on a mat, ankles held down (by a partner or a support), body straight from knees to shoulders.
s: Lean your body forward as slowly as possible, keeping your hips extended.
Resist with your hamstrings.
When you can't hold any longer, put your hands on the floor.
Push the floor with your hands to come back.
nordica.r: Breathe in and let it out slowly during the descent.
nordica.a: 3–5 second descent; you can use your hands to come back.
d: Very effective for preventing hamstring injuries.
Start with few reps.
nordica.c: Causes a lot of muscle soreness at first; start small.

ghr.p: On the glute-ham raise machine, ankles locked in, knees just behind the pad, body straight.
s: Lower your torso forward with your hips extended.
Come up by bending your knees, pulling with your hamstrings.
Finish with your body vertical.
Lower slowly.
ghr.r: Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.
d: A hard exercise; use your hands to help at first.

flexbola.p: Lying on your back, heels on a stability ball, arms on the floor, hips raised with your body straight.
s: Pull the ball toward your butt by bending your knees.
Keep your hips high.
Squeeze your hamstrings.
Straighten your legs back slowly.
flexbola.r: Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.
d: Good for training at home.

v.l.un: Single leg: much harder.

vup.p: Lying on your back, arms straight overhead, legs straight.
s: Raise your torso and legs at the same time.
Try to touch your feet with your hands at the top, forming a V.
Balance on your butt.
Lower slowly.
vup.r: Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.
d: Easier with your knees bent.

v.j.fl: Knees bent: the knees come toward your chest.

rackpull.p: Bar resting on the rack's pins at knee height or just below. Feet hip-width apart, grip just outside your legs, back straight.
s: Brace your abs and take the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor and extend your hips.
Finish standing tall with your glutes squeezed.
Lower the bar back to the pins with control.
rackpull.r: Breathe in and brace your abs before pulling; breathe out at the top.
rackpull.f: Lower back, traps, glutes and grip.
d: Allows more load than a regular deadlift; good for grip and back.
rackpull.c: Protect the rack pins so you don't damage the bar.

v.e.hx: Trap bar: inside the bar, neutral grip.

pant.p: Standing in the machine, shoulders under the pads, balls of your feet on the edge of the platform, heels free.
s: Lower your heels as far as possible, feeling your calves stretch.
Hold for 1–2 seconds at the bottom.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Hold for 1 second at the top and lower slowly.
pant.r: Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.
pant.a: Pause at the bottom and top; slow lowering. No bouncing.
d: The pause at the bottom, with the muscle stretched, is what makes the biggest difference.
10 to 20 reps.

v.p.se: Seated (knees bent): focuses on the soleus, the lower part of the calf.
v.p.lp: On the leg press: balls of your feet on the edge of the platform, push with your ankles only.
v.p.bu: Donkey: torso bent forward; the calf stretches more.
v.e.sm: Smith: a step under the bar.
v.e.ha: Dumbbells: hold one in one hand and rest the other hand on a wall.
v.e.co: Step without load: good for learning or high reps.
v.l.un: Single leg: more load on each side.

corda.p: Standing, feet together, holding the rope with your hands near your hips, elbows close to your body.
s: Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
Jump low, just enough for the rope to pass.
Land on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent.
Keep a steady rhythm.
corda.a: Sets from 30 seconds to a few minutes.
d: Adjust the length: standing on the middle of the rope, the handles reach about your armpits.
corda.c: Start with short sessions if you have shin pain.
